# EDA numbers (generated by `python src/pbl1_eda.py`; do not edit by hand)

Target-related numbers use the training split only (24 train requirements for expected_score; 3,689 train vendors for is_pharmacy).

## E01 Vendors per category

- 4612 vendors, 23 categories, 5439 category memberships (a vendor can be in several).
- Largest: pharmacy 486 (0.1054 of vendors); smallest: pet_supplies 119.
- Category sizes differ by a factor of 4.08; every category is a minority (at most 0.1054 of vendors), so any one-vs-rest classifier faces class imbalance.

## E04 Geography

- Bounding box about 45.5 km (north-south) × 40.8 km (east-west).
- Density is uneven: 0.5690 of vendors lie in the northern half of the box (latitude > 12.8555, the Chennai side) and 0.4310 in the southern half (towards Chengalpattu). See also E12.

## E05 Pincodes

- 106 distinct pincodes; the top 20 hold 2997 vendors (0.6498). 24 pincodes have fewer than 5 vendors.
- Busiest: 603001 (560 vendors). This is why the classifier uses a top-20 pincode one-hot with 'other' as the reference level.
- 1 vendor had no pincode and got its nearest neighbour's.

## E06 Titles

- Median 3 words per title (mean 3.44, max 19). Titles are the only text we have.
- 36 titles (0.0078) contain non-Latin letters (mostly Tamil), which is why normalisation is Unicode-aware.
- 3676 distinct words; 516 appear in at least 5 titles (all vendors; the classifier counts on train only).
- Most common words: shop (568), store (386), and (305), sri (260), chennai (208), stores (197), market (194), pharmacy (189), s (165), ration (146), medicals (125), home (117).

- Radius limits: {1: 5, 3: 7, 5: 10, 10: 8} (km: requirements). 19 of 30 requirements have a preference keyword.
- keyword_in_title is 1 for only 0.0267 of pairs (12 pairs), so its coefficient is the least precise.

## E09 Target distribution (train, 360 pairs)

- Mean 40.03, median 45, sd 33.39, min 0, max 100.
- 0.4194 of scores sit exactly on a rubric anchor; the target is bounded and lumpy, not a smooth Gaussian.
- 0.2472 of train pairs are 'relevant' (≥ 70).

## E10 Category × radius (train)

| category_match | within_radius | mean expected_score | pairs |
|---|---|---|---|
| False | False | 3.75 | 60 |
| False | True | 6.75 | 80 |
| True | False | 48.02 | 121 |
| True | True | 79.16 | 99 |

- Being inside the radius adds 31.15 points when the category matches but 3.00 when it does not: the effects are not additive. A linear (additive) model cannot capture this; kernel ridge can.

## E11 Feature–target correlation (train)

| feature | pearson_r |
|---|---|
| distance_km | -0.227 |
| within_radius | 0.2018 |
| category_match | 0.827 |
| keyword_in_title | 0.1727 |
| n_categories | 0.0353 |
| is_chain | 0.009 |

- category_match dominates; distance is negatively related; is_chain is near 0.

## E12 Nearest-neighbour distance between vendors

- Median 0.044 km, 90th percentile 0.247 km, max 6.165 km; 821 vendors are within 10 m of another (same building / market).
- Half the vendors have a neighbour within this median distance, so in dense areas many candidates sit at almost the same distance and distance alone cannot rank them; category and title matter more.
